hook: Croatia did more of the passing in the final third of the 2018 World Cup Final — and still lost
verified_statistic: Croatia completed 94 of 114 total final-third passes (82.5% field-tilt share) vs France's 20 (17.5%), in a match France won 4-2
plain_english_explanation: Field tilt measures each team's share of completed passes played in the attacking (final) third of the pitch. It is a passing-distribution metric, not a direct measure of territorial control, possession quality, or chance creation.
team_player_match: Croatia vs France, 2018 FIFA World Cup Final, 2018-07-15 (StatsBomb match_id 8658)
comparison_or_baseline: n/a — single-match figure; both teams' full-match completed-pass counts given for context (Croatia 448, France 202)
methodology: locally_calculated. Field tilt = team's completed passes with x>80 (StatsBomb 0-120 pitch, attacking-direction-normalised) / both teams' combined final-third completed passes. metric_id: field_tilt, model_version: event-derived field tilt v1. Reproduced via DuckDB SQL over silver/statsbomb_events (gold/field_tilt_wc2018_final.csv).
confidence: high — simple, fully auditable count over a complete, official event dataset
caveat: Field tilt describes passing distribution, not territory, chance quality, or result. StatsBomb open-data licence requires crediting StatsBomb as source.
suggested_post_copy: Croatia completed 82.5% of the final-third passing in the 2018 World Cup Final. France completed 17.5% — and won 4-2. Field tilt (final-third passing share) isn't the whole story. (Source: StatsBomb Open Data)

hook: Mbappé's World Cup Final volley had a 1-in-10 chance of going in
verified_statistic: Kylian Mbappé's 80th-minute shot (2022 WC Final) carried a StatsBomb xG of 0.102; the nearest opponent captured in StatsBomb's freeze-frame (Molina) was 4.05m away, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez was 15.07m off his line — 8 of Argentina's 11 players on the pitch are captured in this freeze frame
plain_english_explanation: StatsBomb 360 freeze-frame data records the real, tracked positions of players visible around a specific event — here, the instant of the shot. It does not necessarily capture every player on the pitch, so distances describe the nearest CAPTURED opponent, not provably the nearest opponent overall.
team_player_match: Kylian Mbappé (France) vs Argentina, 2022 FIFA World Cup Final, 2022-12-18 (StatsBomb match_id 3869685)
comparison_or_baseline: n/a — single-event spatial snapshot; distances given for all 8 captured opposition players (7 outfield + GK) for context
methodology: locally_calculated from provider-supplied positions (StatsBomb's embedded shot.freeze_frame, not the separate three-sixty file — see caveat). Distance = Euclidean distance, event-anchored spatial_context, NOT continuous tracking. Reproduced via DuckDB SQL (gold/mbappe_360_wc2022_final.csv).
confidence: high for the distances (direct geometry on official freeze-frame data); StatsBomb's xG model output is itself a modelled estimate, not a measured fact
caveat: RECONCILIATION NOTE: StatsBomb carries freeze-frame positions for this shot in two places — the event's own embedded shot.freeze_frame (named players, used for this claim, nearest = 4.05m) and the separate data/three-sixty/{match}.json file keyed by event_uuid (anonymised, nearest = 3.41m for the same event). Both are genuine StatsBomb fields describing the same real players with slightly different coordinates; this pipeline used the embedded field because it carries player identity. Only 8 of Argentina's 11 on-pitch players are captured — never say 'nearest defender' as an absolute. StatsBomb attribution required.
suggested_post_copy: 0.10 xG. The nearest opponent captured in StatsBomb's freeze-frame was 4m away. The keeper was 15m off his line. Mbappé's World Cup Final volley, reconstructed from real tracked positions (8 of 11 Argentina players captured in this frame). (Source: StatsBomb Open Data, 360)

hook: Brisbane Roar's average team width increased by 6.5m in the second half
verified_statistic: Brisbane Roar's average team width in possession went from 39.2m in the 1st half to 45.4m in the 2nd (89 vs 99 possession phases); Adelaide United's went from 48.5m to 43.6m (117 vs 118 phases) over the same match
plain_english_explanation: Team width measures how spread out a side is side-to-side while in possession, averaged across each half's possession phases. This describes the measured width numbers directly — it is not a claim about a formation change or tactical intent, which would need positional/formation evidence this dataset doesn't provide.
team_player_match: Brisbane Roar FC 2-3 Adelaide United FC, A-League 2024/25 (2024-11-23, SkillCorner match_id 1874553)
comparison_or_baseline: 1st half vs 2nd half, same match, both teams
methodology: provider_supplied per-phase width fields (team_in_possession_width_start/end), locally_calculated phase-average per half. Phase-level shape data (snapshots at each possession phase's start/end), not a continuous per-frame trace. Reproduced via DuckDB SQL (gold/skillcorner_team_shape.csv); figures differ by <0.3m from an earlier pandas prototype due to null-row averaging handling — the SQL figures here are the ones of record.
confidence: medium-high — real per-phase provider fields, reasonable sample (423 phases total), but phase-level not frame-level, and width alone does not establish formation or tactical intent
caveat: Describes this one match's width numbers only; does not imply a formation change or tactical explanation. SkillCorner licence: MIT.
suggested_post_copy: Brisbane Roar's average team width in possession went from 39.2m in the first half to 45.4m in the second (width data only — not a formation claim). Still lost 2-3. (Source: SkillCorner Open Data)
